Using the same password for every account
Carrying your Social Security card in your wallet
Sharing account numbers on social media
e: A credit freeze stops new accounts from being opened in your name. It is free.

q: The Truth in Lending Act requires lenders to
o: disclose the APR and total finance charges before a loan is made
offer the lowest rate in the market
e: The Truth in Lending Act requires clear disclosure of credit costs so consumers can compare.

q: Which document will a lender most likely request when you apply for a car loan?
o: Proof of income, such as recent pay stubs
e: Lenders verify capacity to repay with income documents and check credit history.

q: A couple with a new baby depends on both of their incomes. Which insurance need should they review first?
e: When others depend on your income, life insurance replaces it if you die. A new child is a key trigger to review coverage.

q: Which insurance replaces part of your income if an illness or injury keeps you from working?
e: Disability insurance pays a portion of income during a long illness or injury.

q: An inexpensive policy that adds extra liability protection above home and auto coverage is
e: Umbrella policies cover large liability claims, such as lawsuits, beyond your other policies' limits.

q: The amount a policyholder must pay out of pocket before insurance begins to pay a claim is the
e: The premium is what you pay for the policy. The deductible is what you pay per claim before coverage starts.

q: Choosing a higher deductible on an insurance policy usually
o: has no effect on the premium
e: Taking on more of the risk yourself (higher deductible) lowers what the insurer charges.

q: Which type of life insurance lasts your whole life and builds cash value?
e: Whole (permanent) life insurance builds cash value but costs much more than term insurance for the same coverage.

q: The FDIC insures deposits at member banks up to
o: $250,000 per depositor, per bank, per ownership category
the full amount with no limit
e: The FDIC standard limit is $250,000. Credit union deposits get the same protection from the NCUA.

q: Which statement about credit unions compared with banks is most accurate?
o: Credit unions are member-owned not-for-profits and often have lower loan rates
Credit unions are owned by outside shareholders
Credit union deposits are not insured
e: Credit unions return earnings to members through better rates and lower fees. Deposits are insured by the NCUA.

q: Which organization protects customers' securities and cash if their brokerage firm fails?
e: SIPC protects up to $500,000, including $250,000 cash, if a brokerage fails. It does not protect against market losses.

q: A company sells new shares of stock to the public for the first time in the
o: primary market through an initial public offering (IPO).
e: New securities are sold in the primary market. Later trading between investors happens in the secondary market.

q: Which market is used for long-term borrowing and investing, such as stocks and bonds that last longer than a year?
e: Capital markets handle long-term funds. Money markets handle short-term debt of one year or less.

q: A U.S. company exchanges dollars for euros to pay a supplier in Germany. This takes place in the
e: The foreign exchange (forex) market is where currencies are traded.

q: A long period in which stock prices fall 20% or more from their peak is called a
e: A bear market is a drop of 20% or more. A correction is a drop of about 10%. A bull market is a long rise.

q: When interest rates rise, what generally happens to the prices of existing bonds?
e: New bonds pay higher rates, so older bonds paying lower rates become less valuable.

q: An investor buys shares of a Japanese company on a U.S. exchange through an American depositary receipt (ADR). The main added risk is
o: currency risk from changes in the yen-dollar exchange rate
e: Foreign investments carry exchange-rate risk: returns change when currencies move.

q: The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act of 1999 allowed
o: banks, securities firms and insurance companies to combine under one company
e: GLBA repealed parts of the Glass-Steagall Act, allowing financial convergence, and added privacy rules.

q: A company has current assets of $90,000 and current liabilities of $60,000. What is its current ratio?
e: Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities = $90,000 ÷ $60,000 = 1.5.

q: A business has revenue of $400,000, cost of goods sold of $240,000 and operating expenses of $100,000. What is its net income before taxes?
A budget that starts from zero each year and requires every expense to be justified is a
e: Zero-based budgeting makes managers justify every expense instead of adding a percentage to last year's budget.

q: Break-even point in units = fixed costs ÷ (price per unit − variable cost per unit). A food truck has $30,000 in fixed costs, sells meals for $12 and has $7 in variable cost per meal. How many meals must it sell to break even?
e: Contribution per meal = $12 − $7 = $5. $30,000 ÷ $5 = 6,000 meals.

q: A financial manager delays recording expenses so this quarter's profit looks better before a loan review. This is
o: an acceptable way to manage earnings.
e: Manipulating the timing of expenses misrepresents results. Ethics in finance requires honest, accurate reporting.

q: Generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) in the United States are set by the
e: FASB sets U.S. GAAP. The SEC requires public companies to follow it. The IASB sets international standards (IFRS).

q: Which is a key benefit of cloud-based accounting software for a small business?
o: The owner and accountant can see up-to-date records from anywhere
It removes the need for any record keeping
It guarantees the business will be profitable
e: Cloud tools such as QuickBooks Online and Xero give real-time access and automate bank feeds, though data must still be secured.

q: A company's net income is $50,000 on revenue of $500,000. What is its net profit margin?
e: Net profit margin = net income ÷ revenue = $50,000 ÷ $500,000 = 10%.

q: Return on equity (ROE) measures
o: how much profit a company generates with the owners' investment
how much cash is on hand
e: ROE = net income ÷ shareholders' equity. It shows how efficiently owners' money is used.

q: A company's debt-to-equity ratio rises from 0.5 to 2.0 over three years. What does this most likely mean?
o: The company now relies much more on borrowed money and is riskier
The company paid off its debt
e: A higher debt-to-equity ratio means more financing comes from creditors, which raises financial risk.

q: Before deciding to open a new branch, a manager uses budgeting software to see what profit would look like if sales were 10% lower or 10% higher than expected. This is
e: What-if analysis tests how results change under different assumptions.

q: Which technology helps finance teams detect unusual transactions in real time?
e: Machine learning flags transactions that don't fit normal patterns for review.

q: An accountant is asked by her manager to classify a personal expense as a business expense. The most ethical response is to
o: refuse and explain it would misstate the financial records
do it because the manager asked
do it but keep a private note
ask a coworker to do it instead
e: Ethical financial-information management requires accurate records even under pressure.

q: A company reports how much water and energy it saves along with its financial results. This is an example of
o: a non-traditional use of financial information (sustainability reporting).
e: Sustainability and ESG reports connect environmental and social results to financial performance.

q: Which is a responsibility of the financial-information management function?
o: Collecting, analyzing and reporting financial data for decision-making
Setting the Federal Reserve's interest rate
e: FIM turns financial data into useful information for managers, investors and regulators.

q: A lender reviews a client's debt-to-income ratio. If the client earns $6,000 a month and has $2,100 in monthly debt payments, the ratio is
e: Debt-to-income = monthly debt payments ÷ gross monthly income = $2,100 ÷ $6,000 = 35%.

q: A bank requires employees to take at least one week of consecutive vacation each year so someone else handles their work. The main purpose is to
o: uncover fraud that requires daily attention to hide
e: Mandatory vacation is an internal control: schemes often fall apart when someone else does the job.

q: Which is an example of an external risk to a bank?
o: A sudden rise in interest rates
e: External risks come from outside the company (economy, regulation, nature). Internal risks come from inside.

q: Under enterprise risk management, a company's risk appetite is
o: the amount and type of risk it is willing to accept to reach its goals
the total value of its insurance policies
the number of risks it has eliminated
e: Risk appetite guides which risks to accept, reduce or avoid across the organization.

q: The COSO framework is widely used to guide
o: internal control and enterprise risk management
e: COSO publishes the most widely used frameworks for internal control (2013) and ERM (2017).

q: A bank runs a simulated ransomware attack to see how quickly employees respond. This is an example of
o: using technology to test and strengthen risk controls.
e: Testing incident response helps find weaknesses before a real attack.

q: Which law requires the CEO and CFO of a public company to personally certify the accuracy of financial reports?
e: Sarbanes-Oxley (2002), passed after Enron and WorldCom, requires executive certification and internal-control reporting.

q: A financial firm discovers a data breach. Which action is most ethical?
o: Notify affected customers promptly and help them protect their accounts
Wait to see if anyone notices
Blame a vendor publicly before investigating
e: Ethical risk management means transparency and protecting those affected. Most states also require breach notification.

q: Which agency regulates the securities industry and enforces federal securities laws?
e: The SEC protects investors and oversees securities markets. FINRA regulates broker-dealers under SEC oversight.

q: A broker makes excessive trades in a client's account mainly to earn commissions. This illegal practice is
e: Churning puts the broker's commissions ahead of the client's interest.

q: Which agency was created by the Dodd-Frank Act to protect consumers in financial products such as mortgages and credit cards?
e: Dodd-Frank (2010) created the CFPB after the 2008 financial crisis.

q: Under Regulation Best Interest, a broker-dealer recommending an investment to a retail customer must
o: act in the customer's best interest and not put its own interest first
guarantee the investment will make money
e: Reg BI (2020) requires brokers to act in the retail customer's best interest and disclose conflicts.

q: Which retirement account lets an employee contribute pre-tax money directly from a paycheck?
e: Traditional 401(k) contributions reduce taxable income now; withdrawals are taxed in retirement.

q: An investor holds a stock for more than one year before selling it at a profit. The gain is taxed as a
o: long-term capital gain, usually at a lower rate
short-term capital gain at ordinary income rates
e: Gains on investments held more than one year get lower long-term capital gains rates.

q: Banks must report cash transactions over $10,000 to the government to help prevent
e: Under the Bank Secrecy Act, banks file Currency Transaction Reports and suspicious activity reports to fight money laundering.

q: A bank checks a new customer's identity documents before opening an account. This is required by
e: Customer identification programs help stop fraud, money laundering and terrorist financing.

q: Which form of business ownership protects the owners' personal assets from business debts while letting profits pass through to their personal tax returns?
e: LLCs give limited liability with pass-through taxation. Sole proprietors and general partners have unlimited liability.

q: An S corporation differs from a C corporation mainly because an S corporation
o: passes profits through to owners' personal tax returns, avoiding double taxation
e: S corps avoid corporate income tax but are limited to 100 shareholders who must be U.S. citizens or residents.

q: For a contract to be legally binding, which element is required?
o: Offer and acceptance between parties who have legal capacity
A written document in every case
e: Contracts need agreement (offer and acceptance), consideration, capacity and a legal purpose. Many contracts can be oral.
